issues.failure_explanation: The tracking proposition, and the modulus of continuity omega_f, require the whole sequence to stay in K=[-1,1], with f defined only on K. The full residuals L_t lie only in the certified ellipse, whose L-range is about [-2/delta_t, 2/delta_t] and exceeds [-1,1]. This containment is never established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend g_eta continuously to a slightly larger compact interval containing the certified L-range (or use L_t→[-1,1] asymptotically) and rerun the same tracking argument.
issues.overall_effect: The delta*=2 branch of the eta<1 convergence proofs is incomplete as written.
issues.title: Rank-1 convergence for delta*=2 applies the tracking proposition to residuals not shown to lie in K=[-1,1]
issues.why_classification: A local technical extension suffices; the method and the conclusions are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Hereafter, we assume $a_* \ne b_*$ and prove the uniqueness of the positive
definite matrix $P(\delta)$ whose level set contains $x_*$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Lagrange argument constrains a level set only if that set contains an unbalanced stationary point. Nothing in the axioms forces each nested ellipse to meet {ab=1}: small ellipses near the terminal set may avoid it. The conclusion 'the minimizers sweep out (0,2)' presupposes this. The index delta is also redefined from a_*, so P is determined only up to monotone reparametrization, not 'for every delta'. Moreover, A5/A6 hold only for delta ≥ delta_th(eta), yet the family is claimed on all of (0,2).

failure_location.quote:
Consequently, every nonterminal level set
compatible with Axioms~\ref{cond:P_is_pd}--\ref{cond:symmetry} is forced to coincide with the corresponding
level set of the family above.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that every level set with delta ≥ delta_th meets an unbalanced minimizer, state uniqueness up to reparametrization of delta, and restrict the conclusion to the range where A5/A6 hold.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed uniqueness of the scalar certificate, and the derived signal blocks of the rank-1 extensions, are not established as stated.
issues.title: Uniqueness assumes every level set contains an unbalanced minimizer; state labelling is not fixed
issues.why_classification: A comparable conditional uniqueness survives, but the stated scope must be narrowed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: suppose the set of limit points of $(x_t)$ is contained in a finite set $F_\ast\subset\RR^d$
This set is compact but, for $n-1\ge 2$, it contains a continuum of points.

issues.failure_explanation: For rank-1 approximation, the candidate limit set is the union of a minimizer continuum and finitely many non-minimizing points. Lemma lem:finite_limit_set therefore does not apply. Pointwise convergence to a non-minimizing point needs an extra argument, for example that the omega-limit set is connected because increments vanish. This argument is not given.

failure_location.quote:
the preceding finite-limit-set argument yields pointwise
convergence to one of these candidates.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Argue that the omega-limit set of a bounded sequence with vanishing increments is connected. The isolated non-minimizing points are separated from the minimizer component, so convergence to them is pointwise, and the center-stable argument then applies.
issues.overall_effect: The exclusion of non-minimizing stationary limits in the approximation theorem is incompletely justified.
issues.title: Finite-limit-set lemma applied to rank-1 approximation, where the limit set can contain a continuum
issues.why_classification: A short standard connectedness argument closes the gap without changing any claim.

issues.failure_explanation: For mu<0, the gradient factor r+4mu r^3 also vanishes at r^2=-1/(4mu), giving additional stationary curves ab=1±1/(2√(-mu)), e.g. ab=0 or ab=2 for mu=-1/4. So the stationary set differs from that of scalar factorization; only the Hessian at ab=1 matches.

failure_location.quote:
the regime $\mu < 0$, where the stationary set and the Hessian at $ab = 1$
still match those of scalar factorization

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to the Hessian and local structure at ab=1 and acknowledge the extra stationary curves.
issues.overall_effect: The justification offered for applying the certificate locally when mu<0 rests on a false description of the stationary set.
issues.title: False claim that the stationary set matches scalar factorization for mu<0
issues.why_classification: Only an experimental-motivation sentence is affected; no proved result depends on it.
